text: For several days, we painted and read together, or I listened to the wild songs that he played upon his guitar, but nothing could lighten his darkness. <break time="0.8s" /> One of these songs, which he called The Haunted Palace, told of a happy palace whose king was overthrown by evil things. <break time="0.8s" /> Usher believed that the gray stones of his house, along with the still water beside it, had a kind of silent life of their own. <break time="0.8s" /> This silent power, he said, had shaped the fate of his family for centuries and had made him what he now was. <break time="0.8s" /> Having informed me abruptly one evening that the Lady Madeline was no more, he said that he would keep her body for two weeks in a vault. <break time="0.8s" /> He explained that her disease had been unusual, that her doctors were too curious about it, and that the family burial ground was far away. <break time="0.8s" /> Together we carried the coffin down into the deep, damp vault, which had long ago been used for storing gunpowder. <break time="0.8s" /> Only then did I notice how much they looked alike, and Usher told me in a few words that he and his sister had been twins. <break time="0.8s" /> There was still a faint blush upon her face, and a strange, lingering smile was on her lips.
